person: Devon Clarke is the 26-year-old finance manager of a twenty-person community nonprofit. He has been in the job eight months, after working on an audit team. The nonprofit's for-profit social-enterprise LLC, Riverbend Works, bids on government service contracts for workforce training, facilities support and janitorial work. His predecessor left a spreadsheet with tabs named FINAL and FINAL2, and Devon now owns the weekly look at new solicitations. He has never done it alone, and the executive director wants a short list by Monday. He is careful. He wants each rule quoted rather than paraphrased and wants to approve anything that goes to a government portal.
stated_up_front: Hi, I need to go through this week's new federal and county solicitations for Riverbend Works and work out which ones we can actually bid on, and get our questions in before the deadlines. Before you send or keep anything, please tell me which rule you're relying on and let me approve it.

facts.truth: Riverbend Works LLC, wholly owned by the nonprofit, with 20 employees counted across both entities.
561210 facilities support, 561720 janitorial, 611430 training and 561311 employment placement.
Riverbend Works has none of SDVOSB, HUBZone or 8(a). It is registered as a small business only.

facts.about: Bid it cannot keep on size
facts.truth: A janitorial-adjacent bid in a NAICS code with a $5.0M size standard. The $5.32M five-year average is over it.
The janitorial teaming plan on the worksheet gives a large partner, Calloway Facility Group, 65% of the price.
One amendment arrived only by post, dated 2 October 2026. It moves a facilities-support bid from a total small business set-aside to 8(a), and the questions deadline is now 14 October.
One Harlow County bid is reserved for local business enterprises, and Riverbend Works is based in the next county.
Whether the training bid's Section L wants a past-performance reference from within the last three years. The questions deadline is 16 October 2026.
A proposal-writing service at $1,800 per bid and a bid-matching subscription at $249 a month. Both ask for a reply of YES.
Three contracts: a county job-training grant at $410K, a school-district custodial contract at $620K and a workforce program at $280K.

unknowns: Whether the 50 percent limit on subcontracting applies to his teaming plan as a percentage of the price or of the amount paid to the firm
